chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-Mi'za from al-Halabi said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "In the case of a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission), he is given the hadd (flogging) to the extent of what has been freed from him." I asked: "Do you see if half of him is freed, does his testimony become valid in divorce?" He said: "If there is with him a man and a woman, his testimony is valid."

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: A slave who has agreed to pay a specific sum to his master in exchange for freedom, paying in installments.
key_terms.رَجُلٌ وَ امْرَأَةٌ: A man and a woman (referring to the standard composition of witnesses for certain legal acts).
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ: He is subjected to the prescribed flogging (hadd).

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and testimony validity of a partially freed slave (mukatab) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a mukatab’s flogging for breach of contract is proportional to the unpaid portion of his manumission, reflecting the juristic principle of partial liability. Regarding the validity of his testimony in divorce, the Imam specifies that a half-freed slave’s testimony is accepted if accompanied by a man and a woman, aligning with the Quranic standard for witness composition in financial and legal matters. This ruling highlights the nuanced status of the mukatab, who retains certain legal capacities while still bound by his contract.
